summary.headline: Ratnamani Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR1,348 crores, but EBITDA margin was 16.3% amid elevated freight costs; standalone order book above INR2,600 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR1,348 crores, with EBITDA of INR220 crores (16.3% margin) and PAT of INR133 crores. Standalone revenue grew 18% to INR1,104 crores, with EBITDA margin at 12.6%, and the standalone business remains debt-free. Management attributed margin pressure to sharply higher ocean freight, duty and local transport costs on DDP-basis US exports under a 50% tariff, and to lower domestic demand and utilisation. The order book rose about 30% QoQ to over INR2,600 crores, with stainless steel near INR1,000 crores and carbon steel near INR1,700 crores. Management held FY27 standalone guidance of INR4,000-4,200 crores and consolidated guidance of INR5,000-5,200 crores.

segments.name: Ratnamani standalone (stainless and carbon steel)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,104 crores, up 18% YoY, EBITDA margin 12.6%. Stainless steel order book near INR1,000 crores and carbon steel near INR1,700 crores; US exports about 20% of order book.

segments.name: Ravi Technoforge (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue INR99 crores vs INR96 crores a year earlier; EBITDA INR12 crores, margin 11.8%.

segments.name: Ratnamani Finow Spooling Solutions (RFSS, JV)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR157 crores vs INR110 crores a year earlier; EBITDA INR86 crores (54.7% margin); PAT INR65 crores. Order book above INR3,000 crores after a new export order of about INR2,700 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue guidance held at INR4,000-4,200 crores; consolidated INR5,000-5,200 crores, implying a significant H2 ramp-up.
H2 FY27 EBITDA margin expected to improve modestly with utilisation; Q3 margin expected at roughly the same level as Q2.
Freight and tariff-driven cost elevation expected to persist for the next 6-12 months while the 50% US tariff and ocean freight remain.
Next year (FY28) standalone EBITDA margin expected to be upwards of 15%, with utilisation returning to optimum levels.
Long-term consolidated EBITDA margin range of 15-16% to 18% (+/-1%); RFSS long-term EBITDA margin 25-30%.
Middle East hydrocarbon orders expected to convert around middle or end of next year.
capex_capacity: Spiral Mill-3 commissioned: pipes up to 18 metres, annual capacity 100,000 tonnes.
External 3LPE coating plant commissioned at Odisha, annual capacity 25 lakh square metres.
RFSS expansion partly commissioned; induction bend production expected to start next quarter (Q3 FY27).
RFSS full potential revenue INR1,200-1,500 crores at 4,000 tonnes capacity; realisation roughly INR2,500-3,500 per kg, depending on material.
demand_pricing: Stainless steel demand picked up: thermal power, oil and gas (including US LNG), US data centres, chemicals, fertiliser and heat exchangers; competition intensified from players using other process routes.

Carbon steel demand weak domestically for about 9-12 months; US demand strong but tariff at 50% (25% earlier), with DDP pricing embedding duty and freight. Carbon steel pipeline (line pipes and in-plant piping) bidding above INR5,000 crores.
Water segment demand still weak in India due to state government finance pressure; Middle East desalination projects expected to need stainless steel and titanium first, then carbon steel lines.
Fixed-price orders: no pass-through of steel or freight cost increases on existing orders; some detention and demurrage costs under discussion with customers.

Aerospace: five-year global frame agreement signed with Safran for tubes, value rising over years; nuclear orders include HP heater tubes, hairpin heat exchanger tubes, and NPCIL steam generator development order.
Fertiliser: approval to supply stainless steel seamless U-tubes for carbamate condensers from a global licensor and engineering company.

qa_highlights.question: Why did carbon steel volume growth not dent gross margin, and is the margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export DDP pricing embedded freight and duty, so margin looked better; the 35% figure can be taken as a norm over a longer period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consolidated 'other expenses' jump and will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher ocean freight and US duty on DDP orders under 50% tariff; the cost will stay elevated for 6-12 months. Each US order: about INR100 crores FOB, sold at about INR160 crores, with INR60 crores as other expense.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY27 guidance numbers still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Standalone INR4,000-4,200 crores and consolidated INR5,000-5,200 crores are maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Can costs be passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing orders are fixed-price and cannot be repriced; future orders are being priced to reflect costs; detention and demurrage charges under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: What is RFSS realisation and sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation INR2,500-3,500 per kg; current 50% EBITDA margin is sustainable but long-term margin is 25-30%, with quarterly fluctuation.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving working capital build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory and receivables combined run at 5-6 months of business; geopolitical issues delayed some export shipments, and receivables wait for Incoterm transfer, with Abu Dhabi billing and Saudi port shipment.

risks_watch: Ocean freight and geopolitical disruption: freight costs unrecoverable on existing fixed-price orders; H2 and Q3 margins expected flat-to-slightly better.
Working capital: inventory and receivables elevated; cash flow from operations negative in H1 FY27; export deferrals extend the cycle.
US tariff at 50% and about 20% of standalone order book exposed to US; any change in tariff structure affects margin and pricing.
Competitive intensity in stainless steel thermal orders as process-route competitors enter.
Domestic water segment remains weak; state government finances under pressure.
Demand conversion timing: Middle East hydrocarbon tenders expected to convert only in mid-to-late FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order book growth, but cautious on margins: management repeatedly flagged freight, tariff and geopolitical cost pressures as persisting for 6-12 months and was evasive on quantifying the freight and duty impact.
key_quotes: Next year, definitely, we will be somewhere on the upwards of 15%.
Sustainable, but long-term margin should be 25%-30% at EBITDA level.

adds.what: Spiral Mill-3 pipes up to 18 m, 100,000 t/yr annual capacity
External 3LPE coating plant at Odisha, 25 lakh sq m/yr
RFSS expansion: induction bend production (4,000 t capacity; full potential INR1,200-1,500 cr revenue)

growth.why: FY27 standalone guidance of INR4,000-4,200 cr (held, not cut despite the brief's label) and consolidated INR5,000-5,200 cr imply a strong H2 ramp, backed by an order book up ~30% QoQ to over INR2,600 cr plus commissioned Spiral Mill-3 and Odisha 3LPE capacity; utilisation is down due to external factors, and the H2 ramp is not yet backed by specific capacity numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated margin 16.3% and standalone 12.6% in Q2 FY27 with freight/duty costs elevated for 6-12 months; Q3 guided flat to Q2, and FY28 standalone EBITDA guided upwards of 15% vs 12.6% now, so expansion is mainly a FY28 story.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Spiral Mill-3 (100,000 t/yr) and Odisha 3LPE (25 lakh sq m/yr) already commissioned; RFSS induction bend production (4,000 t capacity) guided to start Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone order book up ~30% QoQ to over INR2,600 cr and FY27 standalone guidance of INR4,000-4,200 cr (vs INR1,104 cr revenue in Q2) implies a strong H2 ramp; utilisation currently down on external factors.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond already commissioned capacity; utilisation is down, not near 80%+, so no new capex trigger is supported by the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 standalone INR4,000-4,200 cr and consolidated INR5,000-5,200 cr rather than raising, while flagging freight and tariff cost pressure for 6-12 months.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance requires a steep H2 ramp from H1 run-rate, cash flow from operations was negative in H1, export deferrals extend cycles, and Middle East orders convert only mid-to-late FY28.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: RFSS induction bend production expected to start in Q3 FY27 (4,000 t capacity, full potential INR1,200-1,500 cr revenue); Safran aerospace frame agreement and fertiliser U-tube approval add new product flow.

rows.label: RFSS export order of ~INR2,700 cr
rows.why: RFSS order book now above INR3,000 cr after a new export order of about INR2,700 cr, against Q2 RFSS revenue of INR157 cr, giving multi-quarter visibility.

rows.label: Working capital build-up reversal
rows.why: Inventory and receivables run at 5-6 months of business and H1 FY27 operating cash flow was negative; reversal depends on export shipments and Incoterm transfers that have been delayed.

rows.label: Cost pass-through on future US orders
rows.why: Existing orders are fixed-price with no pass-through, but future orders are being priced for freight and duty, and detention/demurrage recovery is under discussion.

tone.note: Management was confident on order book growth, RFSS and FY27 guidance held, but cautious on margins, repeatedly flagging freight, the 50% US tariff and geopolitics as persisting 6-12 months and evasive on quantifying the freight and duty hit; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, other expenses
